Incident Bot: PAGED: high-error-rate + smart-route fallbacks detected for eu-west edge (alerts: 502 spikes, increased latency) -- paging on-call.

SRE Bot: alert details: 502 count spiked from 0.2% -> 7% in last 3m. SmartRoute fallback count x10. See traces: https://observability/redwood/trace/xyz (obf).

Alex K: i'm seeing a ton of user reports for model failures from eu users. dashboards show traffic being routed to us-west repeatedly, then back to eu, then to ap-south — looks like a routing loop.

Maria P: doing quick DNS check for eu edge vip. dig shows multiple stale A records for vip-edge.eu-west.redwood.internal pointing to old fleet IPs. TTL on those records is still 600s but provider reports they were updated 30m ago.

Maria P:```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> vip-edge.eu-west.redwood.internal A +short
10.4.1.2
10.4.1.2
52.33.120.9  ; old edge node (should be removed)
```

Jenna L: that 52.33.120.9 is from last week's decommission. looks like our external DNS provider didn't purge the rrset consistently across POPs.

Pranay S: checking SmartRoute logs — policy is set to fallback to compatible model variants across regions. I can see fallbacks to model: gptx-8k-quant -> gptx-1-quant because of perceived capacity mismatch. Wrong variant plus stale DNS is causing sessions to break after KV cache miss.

Alex K: so two problems chain: 1) stale DNS endpoints mean requests hit unexpected edge nodes, 2) SmartRoute sees missing capacity and flips variant/regional fallback aggressively, which then causes more failure and more fallbacks. feedback loop.

Liam R: i'm taking pager. @Platform Ops can you open an emergency ticket with DNS provider and request immediate RRset flush for eu-west POPs? Mention TTL inconsistency and rate of 502s.

Platform Ops: on it — opening contact now, ETA for response 6-12m. raising priority.

Eva C: mitigation suggestion: temporarily disable cross-region fallback in SmartRoute for eu-* (set region_fallback=false) and force route to local variant only. This should stop the oscillation while DNS converges.

Pranay S: agree. propose change:
```
SmartRoutePolicy.update({
  region: "eu-*",
  allow_cross_region_fallback: false,
  fallback_limit: 0
});
```

Jenna L: +1 but let's do canary first on eu-west-1 only. we can push a policy patch to eu-west and watch metrics for 2m. if ok, roll to all eu.

Alex K: liability note: disabling fallback may increase 429/over-cap for some customers. call out in thread if we hit any immediate capacity pressure.

Incident Bot: @Liam R assigned as incident lead. Pager escalation timestamp 1919007782.

Liam R: rolling canary now. applying patch to eu-west-1.

SRE Bot: deploy started by deploy-bot. commit: 3a9f4e5 (smartroute: temp-disable-cross-region-eu).

Maria P: DNS provider responded: they acknowledged inconsistency in POP propagation due to cached RRsets at edge CDN — they've queued a global flush for the rrset and say propagation should finish in ~8m. they also recommended decreasing upstream TTL from 600 -> 60 for next week to reduce window.

Pranay S: canary metrics (1m after): fallback_count eu-west-1 down 75%, 502 rate down to 1.4% from 7%. latency stable.

Alex K: good sign. continuing to monitor. @Platform Ops follow-up: ask provider for exact POPs affected and whether they saw partial updates due to their internal cache hierarchy. we need root cause doc for postmortem.

Platform Ops: requesting list now.

Jenna L: also logged customer impact: roughly 18 active customers had increased error rates, top 5 affected are medium-to-large PLG accounts. we should prepare a short customer-facing summary.

Liam R: doing quick impact calc: 18 customers, avg error window 22m, estimated 0.8% of total requests impacted globally but 4-9% in eu mid-peak. SLO threshold breached for 3 customers.

Eva C: creating follow-up runbooks: 1) monitor DNS rrset drift alerts, 2) add TTL-monitoring probe for all active rrsets, 3) limit cross-region fallback chatter (rate limit fallbacks per session), 4) add canary gating for smartroute policy changes.

Incident Bot: note created: INC-2026-1342 (smartroute-dns-propagation-oscillation). assign: Pranay S, Maria P, Platform Ops.

Maria P: provider confirmed flush complete at 1919008200. I'm seeing the stale IP removed from all eu POPs.

Pranay S: rolling the SmartRoute policy change out to all eu regions now (re-enable cross-region fallback after 30m grace and variant mapping fixes).

SRE Bot: policy rollout succeeded. metrics: fallbacks back to baseline, 502s ~0.3%.

Liam R: switching to monitoring-only, handing back to standard on-call at 1919011200. @Alex K can you draft the customer note for the Support team? include timeline, impact, and mitigation steps we took.

Alex K: yep will draft and ping legal for review. brief summary: DNS propagation inconsistency caused stale rrset to direct traffic to decommissioned nodes; that, combined with SmartRoute aggressive fallback to mismatched model variants, created a routing/fallback loop causing elevated errors for eu customers. mitigations: forced DNS rrset flush with provider, canary SmartRoute policy to stop cross-region fallback, rolled policy after verification, and added monitoring/action items.

Incident Bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED by Liam R at 1919011422. Postmortem assigned.

Platform Ops: postmortem action items ticket created: TICKET-4921. items: TTL change to 60s for critical rrsets, add rrset verification in deploy pipeline, add SmartRoute fallback rate-limiter, add alert for stale rrset mismatch.

Jenna L: nice work team. :thumbsup:

Liam R: thanks everyone — leaving notes in the incident doc. I'll follow up tomorrow with a detailed timeline and RCA draft.

Alex K: handing back to normal channel ops.
